Dispatcher for Artificial Feature Generation

Source: R/artificial_features.R
make_artificial_features.Rd

Selects and calls the appropriate artificial-feature generator based on type, returning the augmented predictor matrix together with the column indices of the injected noise block.

Usage

make_artificial_features(
  x,
  n_injected,
  type,
  random_state = NULL,
  knockoff_fallback = c("stop", "allow")
)

Arguments

x

Numeric matrix of predictors (samples \(\times\) features). Must have more columns than n_injected for random permutation; for knockoffs, constructor failure (e.g., rank-deficient input) is governed by knockoff_fallback: by default ("stop") it is an error, and with knockoff_fallback = "allow" a fallback to random permutation is attempted. Fixed-X knockoffs that require row augmentation also fail (or fall back under "allow") because augmented knockoff rows cannot be aligned with the original outcome. All knockoff modes fail closed above 3 000 predictors; random permutation has no such dimensional limit.

n_injected

Positive integer; number of artificial columns to append. Typically round(ncol(x) * artificial_proportion) as computed in stabl_fit().

type

Character string; one of "random_permutation", "knockoff", "knockoff_equi", or "knockoff_mvr".

random_state

Optional integer; passed to set.seed() before any random operations for reproducibility. NULL leaves the RNG unchanged. Seeding happens exactly once in this dispatcher; downstream generators inherit the seeded RNG state and do not re-seed (audit M-5).

knockoff_fallback

Character; the fallback policy when a knockoff constructor fails on a supported-dimensional input (audit A1, strict fallback policy). "stop" (the default) raises an error: a knockoff-to-random-permutation fallback silently changes the FDP+ calibration target, because permutation features do not support FDP+ calibration. "allow" restores the pre-0.2.2 behavior (warn and fall back to random-permutation features for the affected chunk; the fallback_history provenance records the event). The benign knockoff_mvr -> knockoff_equi fallback is unaffected: both are model-X constructions with valid FDP+ calibration, so it remains a warning under either policy.

Value

Named list with three elements:

x_augmented

Numeric matrix of size (nrow(x)) \(\times\) (ncol(x) + n_injected) with the artificial columns appended after the original features.

noise_col_indices

Integer vector of length n_injected containing the 1-based indices into the original x columns (not into the artificial block) that identify which source features were used to build each artificial column. Used by stabl_fit() to look up sparse-group-lasso group memberships for the artificial block via .append_noise_groups.

artificial_provenance

Additive metadata describing the requested artificial-feature type, actual_type used for scientific classification, all generator modes used by the selected artificial columns, and the ordered structured fallback_history. Per-chunk counts and reasons remain available for 0.1.x compatibility.

Details

Injecting artificial features supports STABL's FDP+ diagnostic calibration: by mixing known-noise columns into the predictor matrix alongside real features, STABL can empirically estimate how often a variable of pure noise is selected at a given stability threshold. This observed noise-selection rate drives the FDP+ estimate computed in compute_fdp_plus(). The current rule chooses its minimum and does not imply universal error-rate control.

Four noise strategies are supported:

"random_permutation"

Copies n_injected randomly chosen real columns and shuffles each copy independently, breaking all signal while preserving marginal distributions. Fast and broadly applicable.

"knockoff"

Generates fixed-X knockoffs via knockoff::create.fixed(), which preserve the second-moment (Gram) structure of the original design on the input's own scale: t(xk) xk = t(x) x and t(x) xk = t(x) x - diag(s) with s >= 0 (0.2.2 scale contract). Kept for backward compatibility; note that fixed-X knockoffs are generated once on the full design, so their exchangeability does not survive the row subsampling of the bootstrap loop — prefer "knockoff_equi" or "knockoff_mvr" when correlation structure matters.

"knockoff_equi"

Generates model-X equicorrelated knockoffs via knockoff::create.gaussian(..., method = "equi"). This matches the GaussianSampler(method='equicorrelated') call in Python STABL and is the parity-correct knockoff type for cross-language comparisons.

"knockoff_mvr"

Generates model-X MVR (minimum-variance- reconstructability) knockoffs. The S-matrix is solved by solve_mvr() (an R-native port of knockpy.mrc); sampling uses knockoff::create.gaussian(..., diag_s = S). This is a novel feature exclusive to stablr.

See also

compute_fdp_plus() which consumes the artificial-feature scores, stabl_fit() which calls this function automatically.

Examples

set.seed(1L)
x <- matrix(
  rnorm(20 * 4), 20, 4,
  dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:20), paste0("f", 1:4))
)
generated <- make_artificial_features(
  x, n_injected = 2L, type = "random_permutation", random_state = 1L
)
dim(generated$x_augmented)
#> [1] 20  6
generated$artificial_provenance$actual_type
#> [1] "random_permutation"
try(make_artificial_features(x, 0L, "random_permutation"))
#> Error : `n_injected` must be >= 1.
